clause: We process your personal data only where we have a valid legal basis, including your consent, performance of a contract with you, compliance with a legal obligation, or our legitimate interests.
notes: General statement of Art 6(1) legal bases.

clause: You have the right to withdraw your consent to any processing based on consent at any time, free of charge, and withdrawal will not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before you withdrew it.
notes: Art 7(3) governs withdrawal of consent specifically.

clause: Where we ask for your consent as part of a broader form or agreement, the request for consent is presented separately, in plain and clear language, so it is clearly distinguishable from other matters.
notes: Art 7(2) — consent request must be distinguishable and in plain language.

clause: Our services are not directed at children under 16, and where a child under that age wishes to use services that rely on consent, we require the consent or authorisation of a parent or legal guardian.
notes: Art 8 — conditions applicable to child's consent for information society services.

clause: We do not process data revealing your racial or ethnic origin, health, sex life or sexual orientation unless you have given explicit consent or another exemption under data protection law applies.
notes: Art 9 — processing of special categories of personal data.

clause: Any information about criminal convictions or offences is only processed under the control of official authority or where specifically authorised by applicable law, with appropriate safeguards in place.
notes: Art 10 — processing of personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences.

clause: We collect your personal data only for the specified purposes described in this policy and will not further process it in a manner incompatible with those purposes.
notes: Art 5(1)(b) purpose limitation principle.

clause: We limit the personal data we collect to what is adequate, relevant and necessary for the purposes for which it is processed.
notes: Art 5(1)(c) data minimisation principle.

clause: We take reasonable steps to ensure the personal data we hold about you is accurate and, where necessary, kept up to date, and we will correct or erase inaccurate data without undue delay.
notes: Art 5(1)(d) accuracy principle.

clause: We retain your personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfil the purposes for which it was collected, after which it is securely deleted or anonymised.
notes: Art 5(1)(e) storage limitation principle.

clause: Your personal data is processed in a manner that ensures appropriate security, including protection against unauthorised or unlawful processing and against accidental loss, destruction or damage.
notes: Art 5(1)(f) integrity/confidentiality principle, operationalised by Art 32 security measures.

clause: We are responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate, compliance with these data protection principles across all of our processing activities.
notes: Art 5(2) accountability principle.

clause: We provide information about how we use your personal data in a concise, transparent, intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language.
notes: Art 12 — transparent information, communication and modalities.

clause: When you provide your personal data to us directly, for example by creating an account, we tell you at that time who we are, why we are processing your data, and who else we may share it with.
notes: Art 13 — information to be provided where data is collected from the data subject.

clause: Where we obtain personal data about you from a source other than you directly, such as a business partner, we provide you with information about the processing within a reasonable period, and no later than one month.
notes: Art 14 — information to be provided where data has not been obtained from the data subject.

clause: You have the right to request confirmation of whether we process your personal data and, if so, to obtain a copy of that data along with information about the purposes of processing.
notes: Art 15 — right of access by the data subject.

clause: You have the right to request that we correct any inaccurate personal data we hold about you and complete any personal data that is incomplete.
notes: Art 16 — right to rectification.

clause: You have the right to request the erasure of your personal data where, for example, it is no longer necessary for the purposes for which it was collected or you withdraw your consent.
notes: Art 17 — right to erasure ('right to be forgotten').

clause: You have the right to request that we restrict the processing of your personal data in certain circumstances, such as while we verify the accuracy of data you have contested.
notes: Art 18 — right to restriction of processing.

clause: Where we correct, erase or restrict your personal data, we notify each recipient to whom the data has been disclosed, unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort.
notes: Art 19 — notification obligation regarding rectification, erasure or restriction.

clause: Where processing is based on your consent or a contract and is carried out by automated means, you have the right to receive your personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format and to transmit it to another controller.
notes: Art 20 — right to data portability.

clause: You have the right to object, on grounds relating to your particular situation, to processing of your personal data that is based on our legitimate interests.
notes: Art 21(1) — right to object to processing based on legitimate interests.

clause: You have the right to object at any time to the processing of your personal data for direct marketing purposes, and if you do, we will stop such processing.
notes: Art 21(2)-(3) — right to object to direct marketing.

clause: You have the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal effects concerning you or similarly significantly affects you.
notes: Art 22 — automated individual decision-making, including profiling.

clause: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure and be able to demonstrate that our processing complies with applicable data protection law.
notes: Art 24 — responsibility of the controller.

clause: We implement data protection by design and by default, including by ensuring that only personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed by default.
notes: Art 25 — data protection by design and by default.

clause: Where we determine the purposes and means of processing jointly with another organisation, we set out our respective responsibilities for compliance with data protection obligations in an arrangement between us.
notes: Art 26 — joint controllers.

clause: Where we use third-party service providers to process personal data on our behalf, we enter into a written contract requiring them to process the data only on our documented instructions and to implement appropriate security measures.
notes: Art 28 — processor, incl. required contract terms.

clause: We maintain a record of our processing activities, including the purposes of processing, categories of data subjects and personal data, and the recipients to whom the data has been or will be disclosed.
notes: Art 30 — records of processing activities.

clause: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as encryption and regular testing of our security measures, to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk to your personal data.
notes: Art 32 — security of processing.

clause: In the event of a personal data breach, we notify the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
notes: Art 33 — notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority.

clause: Where a personal data breach is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, we will communicate the breach to you without undue delay.
notes: Art 34 — communication of a personal data breach to the data subject.

clause: Before carrying out processing that is likely to result in a high risk to your rights and freedoms, such as large-scale processing of special category data, we carry out a data protection impact assessment.
notes: Art 35 — data protection impact assessment.

clause: We have designated a Data Protection Officer who can be contacted regarding any questions about how we process your personal data.
notes: Art 37 — designation of the data protection officer.

clause: Our Data Protection Officer is involved in all issues relating to the protection of personal data, reports directly to our highest level of management, and performs their tasks independently.
notes: Art 38 — position of the DPO (involvement, independence, reporting line).

clause: We only transfer your personal data outside the European Economic Area where the conditions set out in data protection law for such transfers are met.
notes: Art 44 — general principle for transfers.

clause: Where we transfer personal data to a country that the European Commission has recognised as providing an adequate level of protection, no further authorisation is required for that transfer.
notes: Art 45 — transfers on the basis of an adequacy decision.

clause: Where we transfer personal data to a country without an adequacy decision, we rely on appropriate safeguards, such as the European Commission's standard contractual clauses, to protect your data.
notes: Art 46 — transfers subject to appropriate safeguards (e.g. SCCs).

clause: You have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority, in particular in the Member State of your habitual residence, place of work, or the place of the alleged infringement, if you consider our processing infringes data protection law.
notes: Art 77 — right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

clause: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of data protection law has the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered.
notes: Art 82 — right to compensation and liability.

clause: For the purposes of this policy, "personal data" means any information relating to an identified or identifiable individual, and "processing" means any operation performed on such data.
notes: Art 4 — definitions.

clause: We may process your contact details on the basis of our legitimate interest to send you marketing communications about similar products; you can object to this processing at any time by using the opt-out link in each communication.
notes: Combines the Art 6(1)(f) legitimate-interest basis with the Art 21 objection right it triggers.

clause: We use cookies and similar tracking technologies; where these are not strictly necessary for the service, we only place them on your device after obtaining your consent in line with applicable consent requirements.
notes: Consent as the GDPR legal basis (Art 6(1)(a)) and the conditions for that consent (Art 7).

clause: In our collection notice, we tell you the period for which your personal data will be stored or, where that is not possible, the criteria used to determine that period.
notes: Art 13(2)(a) disclosure duty for the Art 5(1)(e) storage-limitation principle.

clause: This policy identifies the name and contact details of the controller responsible for your personal data, and, where applicable, of our representative and Data Protection Officer.
notes: Controller identity/contact details are required under both Art 13(1)(a) and Art 14(1)(a).
